name: relative-volume-damped-exposure
rationale: This is the second half of the 2026-09-21 lead #3 test, and it probes a different question from close-location-subsignal. That run established that the TA composite carries approximately zero NET directional information (a total sign flip moved the 500,000 JPY return 0.41pp on a 5.85pp fee drag). 'Zero on average' does not imply 'zero everywhere': the standard decomposition is that a signal computed from a thin, unrepresentative tape is noise, while the same signal computed when the market is actually participating may carry the edge that the average washes out. Shirube has never been able to ask this. Volume is stored on every bar (tickers.volume, aggregated into Candle by TickerRepository::get_aggregated) but reaches neither compute_indicators nor compute_btc_target, and under the CoinGecko series the question was unanswerable by construction: docs/self-improvement-loop.md records that every row carried volume == 1, which is exactly why add-volume-weighted-ma-indicator's 2026-09-07 rejection at sharpe_improvement_pct 0.0 was arithmetic rather than evidence (on constant volume a VWMA IS an SMA). The bitFlyer execution tape has carried real per-minute turnover since 2026-09-09, so this is the first run in which a volume hypothesis can be tested at all, and re-testing an idea the doc itself flags as never fairly tested is a better use of a slot than another knob on the dead gain axis. The mechanism is deliberately conservative and is NOT another gain knob: instead of scaling the composite by a fitted constant, it pulls the composite toward its own neutral point 0.5 by an amount determined entirely by an OBSERVABLE -- the bar's volume relative to a trailing median of the same series -- so that on a bar whose turnover is at or above the trailing median the composite passes through completely unchanged, and only bars in the thin tail are damped. That asymmetry matters: it means the variant cannot differ from the baseline on a normal bar, so any measured difference is attributable to the thin tail specifically rather than to a uniform amplitude change, which is what separates this from the whole zone-damping family. Secondary and explicitly not the motivation: because thin minutes are also the minutes where the realised spread and slippage are worst, damping there should reduce the number of low-quality round trips, which is relevant to seven consecutive runs of negative sharpe_minus_static_mix -- but it is scored on the promotion rule like everything else, and a turnover reduction that does not clear Sharpe is a rejection.
code_change_summary: Expose each bar's turnover relative to a trailing baseline on IndicatorPoint, and use it in TradingEngine::compute_btc_target to pull the aggregated composite toward 0.5 on thin bars only. Three edits. (1) In src/signal/mod.rs, add one field to IndicatorPoint -- `pub rel_volume: Option<f64>` -- with an English doc comment stating it is the bar's volume divided by the trailing median volume of the preceding RELVOL_WINDOW bars, that it is None until that window is full, and that a non-positive or missing trailing median also yields None so the consumer treats it as 'no information' rather than as zero. In compute_indicators(), maintain a fixed-capacity rolling buffer of the last RELVOL_WINDOW = 60 bars' volumes (60 one-minute bars = one hour of turnover; chosen as the smallest window that spans a full hour at the resolution this pipeline runs at, NOT tuned -- see constraints) and set rel_volume = current_volume / median(previous 60 volumes), computed from the PRECEDING bars only so the value is strictly causal and never reads its own bar. Use the median, not the mean, because per-minute crypto turnover is heavy-tailed and a single burst minute would otherwise suppress the following hour. Take volume from the same Candle the existing close is read from, via the identical Decimal -> f64 path. Do not change how any indicator is constructed, updated or reset. Update every other IndicatorPoint construction site to the new struct shape in the least invasive way (None where no Candle history is in hand; ..Default::default() in test constructors if the struct derives Default). (2) In TradingEngine::compute_btc_target (src/trading/engine.rs), after `ta_normalized` is computed by the existing weighted mean and BEFORE it is combined with sentiment, apply one damping step through a new named private helper with a doc comment giving the formula and its range -- e.g. `fn volume_conviction(rel_volume: Option<f64>) -> f64 { match rel_volume { Some(r) if r.is_finite() && r >= 0.0 => r.min(1.0), _ => 1.0 } }` and then `let ta_damped = 0.5 + (ta_normalized - 0.5) * volume_conviction(raw.rel_volume);`, using ta_damped in the `combined` expression. The clamp at 1.0 is what makes the damping one-sided: a bar at or above its trailing median volume has conviction exactly 1.0 and is passed through BIT-IDENTICALLY to the baseline, an above-median bar is never amplified, and only a bar below its trailing median is pulled toward 0.5 in proportion to how thin it is. A None rel_volume (warmup, or a non-positive trailing median) MUST also yield conviction 1.0, i.e. the pre-change behaviour, so that warmup bars are untouched. Because ta_normalized is in [0.0, 1.0] and the conviction factor is in [0.0, 1.0], ta_damped is in [0.0, 1.0] too and the function's range guarantee is preserved by construction -- state that in a comment. Document the change with a NOTE comment naming this hypothesis and stating the mechanism under test. (3) Nothing else. Do NOT change any sub-signal's formula, damped_cross, CROSS_SATURATION, either family weight, the family weight each sub-signal is pushed with, the weighted-mean aggregation or its divisor, the empty-sub_signals warmup guard, the sentiment path, the ta_weight/sentiment_weight combination, or the final clamp. Add unit tests in src/trading/engine.rs: (a) rel_volume = Some(1.0) and rel_volume = Some(3.0) both returning EXACTLY the pre-change composite for a fixed bullish point (the one-sided pass-through pin, asserted with an exact equality, not an epsilon); (b) rel_volume = None returning that same pre-change composite (the warmup pin); (c) rel_volume = Some(0.0) on a strongly bullish point returning exactly ta_weight * 0.5 + sentiment_weight * 0.5 (full damping to neutral); (d) rel_volume = Some(0.5) returning a composite strictly between (c)'s and (a)'s, and monotone in rel_volume across 0.0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1.0; (e) a mirror bearish point asserting the damping pulls UP toward 0.5 rather than always down, i.e. it is neutral-seeking and not directional; (f) an all-None IndicatorPoint asserting the warmup guard still returns None before any damping is reached. Add unit tests in src/signal/mod.rs asserting rel_volume is None for the first RELVOL_WINDOW bars, that it equals the expected ratio on a hand-computed case, that it uses the median rather than the mean on a deliberately skewed buffer, and that it never reads its own bar's volume. Update any existing compute_btc_target_* test whose expected value legitimately changes, and do not weaken or delete a test to make it pass. Additionally instrument and REPORT (stderr logging or a scratch harness ONLY -- do NOT add a field to BacktestReport) the distribution of the conviction factor over the evaluated window: the fraction of evaluated bars at conviction exactly 1.0 (pass-through), the mean conviction, and the fraction below 0.5. If nearly every bar passes through at 1.0 the variant is close to inert and the coordinator must be told that rather than left to read a null result as a verdict on the idea.
constraints: This hypothesis DOES modify TradingEngine::compute_btc_target's body. That is permitted under experiments/hypotheses/README.md's '`compute_btc_target` may be modified' section, but ONLY on this hypothesis's own dedicated isolation: "worktree" branch, and it MUST be reported explicitly so the coordinator flags it in any PR description.
MUST NOT change compute_btc_target's SIGNATURE. Only its body may change.

MUST NOT change any sub-signal's formula, damped_cross, CROSS_SATURATION, REVERSION_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT, TREND_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT, the family weight each sub-signal is pushed with, the weighted-mean aggregation or its divisor, the empty-sub_signals warmup guard returning None, the sentiment normalization, the ta_weight/sentiment_weight combination, or the final clamp. The ONLY behavioural change is one volume-conditioned damping of the aggregated composite toward 0.5.

The damping MUST be one-sided and MUST NOT amplify: conviction is capped at 1.0, so a bar at or above its trailing median volume is passed through bit-identically to the baseline. A missing or non-finite rel_volume MUST also mean conviction 1.0, never 0.0 -- absent information must never be read as 'thin'.
MUST NOT touch apply_zone, sticky_target, block_start, allocation_delta_to_order, the lot-size check, the orders_below_min counting arm, the RiskManager call sequence, or the fee logic.

RELVOL_WINDOW is fixed at 60 bars and MUST NOT be tuned, swept or fitted -- not on the holdout window and not on any other window. It is one hour of bars at this pipeline's 60s resolution, chosen for that reason alone. If a different window looks better, that is a separate hypothesis to propose, not a value to change mid-run. Likewise the conviction mapping introduces no fitted constant: it is min(rel_volume, 1.0), not a scaled or exponentiated form.

The relative-volume baseline MUST be strictly causal -- computed from bars STRICTLY PRECEDING the current one, never including the current bar's own volume, and never from any future bar. A lookahead here would silently invalidate the entire run, so it carries its own unit test.

MUST pass `cargo test`, including every existing compute_btc_target_* unit test. Update an expected value only where the damping legitimately changes it, and do not weaken or delete a test just to make it pass.

MUST NOT change src/signal/engine.rs's broadcast cadence or anything about live scheduling. Adding a field to IndicatorPoint and populating it is permitted; changing when or how often an IndicatorPoint is produced is not. NOTE for the implementing agent: if the LIVE path builds IndicatorPoint somewhere that has no rolling volume history available, populate rel_volume as None there rather than inventing a substitute, and REPORT that asymmetry between the live and backtest paths to the coordinator -- it would mean the variant is a no-op live even if it scores well in backtest, which is a finding in its own right and must not be papered over.

A promoted change still becomes its own PR against dev (per the pipeline's step 6) and is never merged automatically -- a human reviews it like any other algorithm hypothesis. Flag explicitly in the PR description that this diff touches compute_btc_target's body and conditions the allocation target the live engine acts on on a newly-introduced observable.
MUST NOT touch src/exchange/bitflyer/*, .github/workflows/*, or the order-submission mechanics themselves.
